title: APA Practice Guideline for Borderline Personality Disorder: psychotherapy and medication
fact: The 2024 APA guideline recommends (1B) that patients with borderline personality disorder receive a structured psychotherapy that has literature support and targets the core features of the disorder; the pages seen do not name DBT or MBT specifically, and the guideline lead stated no therapy emerged as a gold standard. For medication, it suggests (2C) that psychotropics be time-limited, aimed at a specific measurable target symptom, and adjunctive to psychotherapy, with medications reviewed at least every 6 months (1C).
source: American Psychiatric Association. Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Borderline Personality Disorder. Washington DC: APA; 2024 (news release 10 Dec 2024).
note: Verified on the psychiatryonline guideline page and APA news release. Specific therapies (DBT, MBT) were NOT named on the pages opened; do not add them to the box unless the full text is checked. Release page: https://www.psychiatry.org/News-room/News-Releases/Updated-Borderline-Personality-Disorder-Guideline

title: NICE NG222 Depression in adults: CBT and behavioural activation
fact: NICE (June 2022) advises discussing treatment options and matching them to the person's needs and preferences. For less severe depression, its rationale cites good evidence for group CBT and group behavioural activation, with individual CBT, individual BA or guided self-help as alternatives, and guided self-help as the least intrusive option to consider first. For more severe depression, the rationale cites good evidence for individual CBT and individual behavioural therapies, and for CBT combined with an antidepressant.
source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Depression in adults: treatment and management. NICE guideline NG222. Published 29 June 2022.
note: Seen: rationale page and recommendations 1.5.2, 1.5.3, 1.6.1 in the PDF (published 29 June 2022). The rationale for more severe depression says 'individual behavioural therapies', not BA by name. Last-updated date not seen.

title: 2023 VA/DoD PTSD guideline synopsis: trauma-focused psychotherapies
fact: The synopsis of the 2023 VA/DoD guideline recommends specific manualized trauma-focused psychotherapies, namely prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, or EMDR, over pharmacotherapy. The abstract says six PTSD treatment recommendations were rated strong but does not say which, so the strength for each therapy is not confirmed here.
source: Management of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Acute Stress Disorder: Synopsis of the 2023 U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and U.S. Department of Defense Clinical Practice Guideline. Ann Intern Med. 2024;177(3):363-374. doi:10.7326/M23-2757
note: Confirmed from the PubMed abstract record (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38408360/). The healthquality.va.gov guideline page was blocked, so per-therapy strength is unverified.

title: APA (American Psychological Association) 2025 PTSD guideline update
fact: The updated guideline, approved by the APA Council in February 2025 per Monitor on Psychology, lists CPT, prolonged exposure and trauma-focused CBT as 'recommended'. EMDR, cognitive therapy and narrative exposure therapy are 'suggested', on a weaker evidence base. It favors psychotherapy over medication, suggesting SSRIs or SNRIs as second-tier options.
source: American Psychological Association. Guidelines for treating PTSD and trauma. Monitor on Psychology. 2025;56(5) (July/August 2025).
note: Seen via the Monitor news article, not the guideline document itself. Wording 'recommended'/'suggested' is the article's description. Note a published critique of this guideline exists (Northumbria/QUB portals), not opened. Contrast: VA/DoD 2023 lists EMDR alongside PE and CPT.

title: Bio- and neurofeedback for depression meta-analysis (and neurofeedback for ADHD, 2025)
fact: A 2022 meta-analysis found that heart rate variability biofeedback and neurofeedback were associated with lower self-reported depression, but the authors noted the controversy and the limited research quality, and that benefits rested mainly on self-report. For ADHD, a 2025 JAMA Psychiatry meta-analysis of 38 RCTs found no significant improvement on probably blinded symptom ratings (SMD 0.04, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.18) and concluded neurofeedback did not appear to meaningfully benefit people with ADHD at the group level.
source: (1) Fernandez-Alvarez J, et al. Efficacy of bio- and neurofeedback for depression: a meta-analysis. Psychol Med. 2022;52(2):201-216. doi:10.1017/S0033291721004396. (2) Westwood SJ, et al. Neurofeedback for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. JAMA Psychiatry. 2025;82(2):118-129. doi:10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2024.3702
note: Westwood seen via the iris.unica.it repository record (PubMed was behind a captcha); Fernandez-Alvarez via the Maastricht CRIS record: https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291721004396. Two separate items; split into two boxes if preferred. Standard-protocol-only ADHD result was small (SMD 0.21, CI 0.02 to 0.40).

title: Hypnosis: umbrella review and IBS network meta-analysis
fact: A 2024 review of 49 meta-analyses (261 primary studies) found the strongest hypnosis evidence for medical procedures and pain, but only 9 of the 49 meta-analyses were rated high quality. A 2024 network meta-analysis found face-to-face gut-directed hypnotherapy modestly reduced IBS abdominal pain (RR of non-improvement 0.77, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.96), with mostly low to very low certainty.
source: (1) Rosendahl J, Alldredge CT, Haddenhorst A. Meta-analytic evidence on the efficacy of hypnosis for mental and somatic health issues: a 20-year perspective. Front Psychol. 2024;14:1330238. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238. (2) Goodoory VC, et al. Effect of Brain-Gut Behavioral Treatments on Abdominal Pain in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis. Gastroenterology. 2024;167:934-943. doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2024.05.010
note: Second DOI: https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2024.05.010 (seen in the White Rose repository PDF). The Rome working team report found (Keefer 2022, Gastroenterology 162(1):300-315, doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2021.09.015) is real, but the page did not state hypnotherapy conclusions, and no 2023 Rome hypnotherapy report was found, so it is not used.
